question: In a trauma patient, the presence of blood at the urethral meatus is an absolute contraindication to insertion of a urethral catheter without prior urological assessment.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Blood at the urethral meatus is an absolute contraindication to urethral catheterisation until urethral injury has been excluded. This is a critical ATLS principle.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Blood at the urethral meatus indicates possible urethral disruption (commonly associated with pelvic fractures). Blind catheterisation in this setting risks converting a partial urethral tear into a complete one. A suprapubic catheter or retrograde urethrogram must be considered first.
